newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end up on strong technical rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end up on strong technical rally.

text.p: U.S. debt futures shrugged off an early weight of conflicting economic data and news reports to rally in the final minutes of pit trading to new highs.

December 30-year U.S. Treasury bond futures broke through major resistance levels to establish a new nine-month high of 115-25/32. Pit traders said momentum, carried over from Tuesday, points to a challenge of resistance at 116-08/32.

"We had a sneaky bid to this stuff all day. Once these unnamed Fed officials stopped talking ... it went through some levels and it was pretty stratospheric," one trader said, adding buyers in the late rally were "a cast of thousands."
Traders said the rally got going on a positive market reaction to a U.S. Treasury auction on Wednesday afternoon of $12.504 billion in five-year notes.

Traders said the auction's bid-to-cover ratio of 2.86 looked better than recent figures. The auction produced a high yield of 5.950 percent, non-U.S. institutional buying of $1.32 billion and non-competitive bids totalling $310 million.

The auction moved December T-bonds off mid-morning lows set in the wake of heavy selling overnight in European markets, news reports of U.S. Federal Reserve officials' inflation views and a wider September U.S. trade deficit.

The September trade gap had been expected to narrow to $9.5 billion, according to a Reuters poll. But the Commerce Department reported early Wednesday that it grew 10.1 percent in September to $11.34 billion versus an August figure revised down to $10.30 billion from $10.83 billion.
Total U.S. exports fell 1.4 percent to $68.79 billion in September, while imports rose 0.1 percent to $80.13 billion, the Commerce Department reported.
Some analysts pointed to higher prices and import volumes for oil as contributing to the wider trade gap. One bond futures pit trader said the oil data was a bearish indicator.
A Federal Reserve source told Reuters Tuesday that the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee at its September 24 meeting "came very close to raising rates."
Later wire reports quoted Fed sources as saying that any policy move is more likely to be a tightening than an easing.

Both reports were bearish on debt markets shortly after the opening and temporarily blunted any momentum from Tuesday, as did slumping European markets keying off of German money supply figures, traders said.
Looking ahead, a technical analyst said December T-bonds were likely to test 116-1/2 to 117-1/2.

At the end of pit trading, December T-bonds were up 16/32 to 115-23/32, December 10-year notes were up 09/32 to 111-01/32 and March Eurodollars were up 0.01 to 94.51. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
